hypothesis: data scale, not label or coupling: does the F1 mirror toward-the-gap rate become non-zero when the F1 curriculum grows from six groups to twelve or more?

split.rule: groups are ordered R18/R19 F1 order then acceptance order; index even -> train, odd -> held-out; the frozen R19 validation groups are forced held-out; while train < 12 and held-out > 5 the last held-out group is flipped to train (and, if held-out < 5, the last train group is flipped back).  Mirrors are atomic: a group never crosses the split

assertions.note: the small arm deliberately trains on all six old F1 groups, which includes the three frozen R19 validation groups; its r19-frozen reading is therefore a seen reading and is never used for a held-out claim

rule.P1: on the NEW held-out set, the large arm's flip count per seed over the need-left cells (the gap is screen-left of the player at the start, so the screen-right prior is wrong); scale_helps iff at least two of three seeds are > 0, scale_not_the_cause iff all three are 0, partial_scale otherwise
rule.P1_mirror: the mirror-only subset of the need-left cells, reported separately; it is the exact analogue of round19/24's mirror group, but the new held-out also contains base cells the prior gets wrong
rule.P2: base survives iff the large arm's keep rate over the need_right cells (where screen-right is correct) is >= 0.5 in every seed
rule.P3: the R19-frozen set is reported for both arms against round24's recorded arm A; its three need-left cells are exactly the three mirror events, so its flip count is directly comparable to round24's mirror toward count of 3/9
rule.geometry: the new held-out set mixes gap sides, so a RAW "mirror toward" rate can be satisfied by the frozen screen-right prior: the baseline B0 itself scores 5/7 mirror-toward there (and 2/7 base-toward).  The primary is therefore direction-conditioned, and the raw mirror/base toward counts are reported as a caveat, never as the verdict
rule.overall: scale_helps iff P1 == scale_helps and P2 holds; mixed_scale iff P1 == scale_helps and P2 fails; scale_not_the_cause iff P1 == scale_not_the_cause; partial_scale otherwise

judgement.claim_limit: descriptive counts over three seeds and seven new held-out F1 groups; mirrors are not independent samples; no significance test is run

round24_reference.note: round24 arm A on exactly the six R19-frozen F1 validation events

environment.note: recorded inside the run; both TF32 flags must read false

limitations: the small arm trains on all six old F1 groups, which includes the three frozen R19 validation groups; its r19-frozen numbers are seen numbers, and every primary claim uses the new held-out set
the two arms are not nested: S = the six old groups, L = three old train groups plus nine new groups, so size and composition change together
seven new held-out groups (14 cells, 7 base + 7 mirror per network); mirrors are not independent samples and three seeds are not independent runs of the world
updates are fixed at 200, so the small arm sees 16.7 epochs and the large arm 8.3: compute is held fixed, not epochs
F1 success is a 12-20 px parking window reached before a fixed lethal frame; it is a geometric construction, not tactical play
the teacher labels come from a planner that is told the world geometry, not from a learned policy
synthetic fixed-y worlds, two-frame actions, no shooting, no bombs, no real TH08 pixels or hitbox
one hyper-parameter configuration; no tuning; no formal gate; no deployable checkpoint
